framework: LangChain; MetaGPT; AutoGen; CAMEL; CrewAI; LangGraph
failure_observed: A single atomic false claim seeded in one agent spreads through message dependencies and hardens into system-wide false consensus; injected seeds infect up to 100% of runs.
locus_detail: endogenous: tracer seed in the entry/hub agent system directive; exogenous: application-layer message injection at high-influence (hub, aggregator) agents
evaluation: QUANT (UCI), RIGID (MATH-style) and MMLU-retrieval tasks; ASR, BICR, safe completion, tokens per safe run; 6 frameworks in 3 topologies; agent backbone model not identified in sections read
limitation: Binary adoption criterion may miss partial internalization; spectral indicator R is a heuristic; adaptive multi-stage adversaries out of scope; defense adds latency.
evidence_note: trigger: "Endogenous Stochastic Errors" emulated by a tracer seed (§IV-A, Fig. 4) and "Exogenous Strategic Adversary" injection (§V, Table IV); trigger_evidence_level: seed in entry agent system prompt vs attacker message injection, not shown at one identical step, so narrower value; locus: seed prefixed to target agent system directive (App. C) and injected messages (§V); spread: S(t) coverage rises, five of six frameworks reach 100% final infection (Fig. 4, Table I); defense_family: Lineage Graph provenance plus tri-state claim verification and rollback (§VI); defense_evaluated_against: Tables V-VII use attacker policies only; abstract claim of endogenous suppression has no matching defense table
review_note: Abstract says defense suppresses endogenous errors, but Table V is attack-only; coded adversarial. Released artifact is code, datasets and scripts (anonymous link); not clearly failure traces, coded no.

failure_observed: Adversarial content accepted at one stage is forwarded as trusted input across unverified inter-agent boundaries (content injection, consensus poisoning, plan hijacking, Sybil substitution); attack success 0.6-0.86 on every backbone.
locus_detail: retrieved web content (A1), sub-agent result at orchestrator aggregation (A2), planner decomposition (A3), routing-slot agent identity (A4) in a 10-agent five-layer pipeline
evaluation: 147 annotated TRAIL traces (GAIA, SWE-Bench Lite) for threat derivation; 1,080 attack runs plus 90 clean on 20 tasks, 4 attacks x 3 variants; attack success, accuracy, recovery rate, hop count; GPT-5-mini, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Kimi K2.5
limitation: Reviewer: one custom pipeline and 20 tasks; boundary verification is argued for but never implemented or tested; benign trace evidence comes from a different system than the attack runs.
evidence_note: trigger: failures in 147 benign TRAIL traces (§III) and injected attacks A1-A4 in a controlled pipeline (§IV); trigger_evidence_level: benign traces come from a GAIA CodeAgent system, attacks from the authors 10-agent pipeline, so different systems, narrower value; locus: content, delegation and identity boundaries (§II.B, §III); spread: payloads traverse 4-6 hops under A1 and A2 (Fig. 6d)
review_note: Considered direct-both (same boundary classes benign and adversarial) but the two sets of runs are on different systems. No defense is tested; boundary verification is only a proposed primitive.

framework: ChatDev; MetaGPT; HyperAgent; AppWorld; AG2; Magentic-One; OpenManus
failure_observed: MAS runs fail (41-86.7% failure rates) through 14 modes in three groups: system design issues, inter-agent misalignment and task verification.
locus_detail: varies by failure mode: agent role or task specification, inter-agent messages, verifier or termination step
evaluation: MAST-Data 1642 annotated traces from 7 MAS on ProgramDev, SWE-Bench Lite, GSM-Plus, GAIA and others; failure-mode prevalence, kappa; GPT-4 and Claude series; intervention case studies on AG2 and ChatDev
limitation: Taxonomy is not claimed exhaustive; some failures stem from base-LLM limits; interventions are not universal and effects vary by LLM.
evidence_note: trigger: failures arise in unmodified runs of 7 MAS, no adversary (§2, Table 1); trigger_evidence_level: no attack condition anywhere; defense_family: prompt and role refinement, added Verifier role (App. H.1, H.2); defense_evaluated_against: AG2 MathChat and ChatDev benchmarks with success rates (Table 5, App. H)
review_note: Locus coded not reported because it differs per failure mode. detection_method trace-analysis is an LLM annotator that labels modes per trace rather than naming a failing agent; judgment call. Spread not measured as agent-to-agent movement.

framework: Self-collab; MetaGPT; Camel; SPP; MAD; AgentVerse
failure_observed: An agent that makes injected or self-generated mistakes degrades multi-agent performance; drop is 5.5% for hierarchical, 10.5% and 23.7% for the other structures.
locus_detail: the faulty agent whose profile is rewritten (AutoTransform) or whose messages are corrupted (AutoInject), e.g. code writer, task distributor
evaluation: HumanEval code generation, CIAR math, CommonMT translation and a text-evaluation task; accuracy and BLEURT; GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o; 6 multi-agent systems in linear, flat and hierarchical structures
limitation: Authors note AutoTransform cannot control error count or type; Reviewer: errors are LLM-injected and may not match natural faults.
evidence_note: trigger: "AutoTransform and AutoInject ... introduce mistakes into the agents responses" (§3); trigger_evidence_level: only error injection studied, no separate attack setting; locus: faulty agent output (§3, Table 1); spread: performance drop differs by structure and by higher-level distributors (§4.1, §4.4), only final performance measured; defense_family: Challenger and Inspector agent (§5); defense_evaluated_against: Fig. 3 and Table 3 under AutoInject and AutoTransform errors
review_note: Abstract and intro call faulty agents clumsy or malicious; AutoTransform builds stealthy erroneous agents. Coded benign-bug under the fault-injection rule; plausible alternative is both. Abstract says code and data are available; unclear if traces, coded no.

failure_observed: Byzantine agents sending erroneous messages corrupt consensus in LLM-based networks of 7 nodes across topologies, with up to 6 faulty nodes.
locus_detail: Byzantine nodes (weaker LLM) at random positions, or at the center versus a leaf of a star
evaluation: GSM8K and XSTest, 10 questions each; round-level accuracy; GPT-4o-mini vs GPT-3.5-turbo and LLaMA3.1-8B vs LLaMA3-8B; 7-node networks in 6 topologies, 1-6 Byzantine nodes
limitation: Reviewer: 10 questions per task and strong-weak model pairs stand in for Byzantine behavior.
evidence_note: trigger: Byzantine agents implemented as a weaker model paired with a stronger one (§Pilot, App. A), no adversarial prompting seen; trigger_evidence_level: single fault model; locus: center versus leaf malicious nodes (Fig. 2, Table 1); defense_family: CP-WBFT confidence-probe weighted consensus (§Method); defense_evaluated_against: Tables 2-3 with 6 of 7 Byzantine nodes of the weak-model kind
review_note: Paper calls these agents malicious/Byzantine but they are weak-model nodes; coded benign-bug, alternative adversarial. Spread not reported: topology effects are shown on accuracy, not on movement between agents.

failure_observed: A self-replicating malicious prompt hops across agents like a virus, causing data theft, scams, content manipulation and malware, even with local messaging.
locus_detail: malicious prompt in an email, PDF or web page read by the first tool agent, then replicated in agent-to-agent messages; in the society, one compromised citizen agent
evaluation: 120 instructions x 3 tool types, 360 instruction-attack pairs; attack success rate; GPT-4o and GPT-3.5 Turbo; pipelines with global vs local messaging; societies of 10-50 agents
limitation: Reviewer: simulated injections (web content injected in simulation), two OpenAI models, simple tagging defense.
evidence_note: trigger: "Prompt Infection" adversary embeds a self-replicating prompt (§3, §4); trigger_evidence_level: no benign fault condition; locus: payload in external content then inter-agent messages (Fig. 2, §4.1); spread: infected agents grow exponential then logistic with population size (Fig. 6a, §5.2); defense_family: LLM Tagging plus repurposed marking and delimiting defenses (§6); defense_evaluated_against: defense experiments run on the same attacks (§6)
review_note: Defense results were read only briefly; LLM Tagging coded provenance-authorization since it labels message origin.

failure_observed: Injected semantic faults (hallucination, misread instructions, reasoning drift, blind trust) propagate silently; linear workflows collapse while closed-loop designs neutralize over 40% of faults.
locus_detail: faults injected by prompt modification and response rewriting at an agent, and by message-routing manipulation between agents
evaluation: HumanEval, WikiTableQuestions (400 sampled), WebShop; 15 fault types; recovery and fault-tolerance rates; GPT-5 and DeepSeek-V3; 3 MAS architectures
limitation: Reviewer: three systems, single-trial Pass@1, faults produced by GPT-5-mini.
evidence_note: trigger: controlled fault injection to simulate semantic errors (§3.2, §4.1.2); trigger_evidence_level: no adversary modeled; locus: three injection mechanisms prompt, response, routing (§3.2); spread: MetaGPT linear pipeline drops to 0.0% under Blind Trust as errors propagate downstream unchecked (§4)
review_note: Fault-tolerant behavior taxonomy describes what existing systems do, not a proposed defense; defense none. n_agents not stated in sections read.

failure_observed: Which agent and which step cause a multi-agent task failure is hard to find; best attribution method gets 53.5% agent accuracy and 14.2% step accuracy.
locus_detail: failure-responsible agent and decisive error step in each failure log
evaluation: Who&When: 184 annotated failure tasks from 127 systems on GAIA and AssistantBench; agent-level and step-level accuracy; GPT-4o, o1, DeepSeek R1; 3 attribution methods
limitation: Authors: even reasoning models are not practically usable; Reviewer: annotation uncertainty of 15-30% by annotator.
evidence_note: trigger: logs of agent mistakes in task runs, no adversary (§3); trigger_evidence_level: benign only; locus: annotated failure-responsible agent and decisive step (§2, §3.1)
review_note: system_type left not reported: generated teams are unspecified and Magentic-One is only described as five specialized agents. Mechanism not coded because the paper labels who/when, not how.

failure_observed: Framework-level bugs in CrewAI and LangGraph, mostly API misuse, API incompatibility and documentation desync, show up as functional errors, crashes and build failures.
locus_detail: agent framework code across lifecycle stages; most bugs in the Self-Action stage
evaluation: 998 issue reports from CrewAI and LangGraph; taxonomy of 15 root causes and 7 symptoms over 5 lifecycle stages
evidence_note: trigger: "empirical study of 998 issue reports" of framework bugs (abstract); trigger_evidence_level: bug reports only, no adversary (abstract)
review_note: scope: possible; bugs concentrate in the Self-Action stage, so multi-agent relevance is unclear from the abstract. No PDF available.

failure_observed: LLM agents can hide unauthorized information sharing from monitors through steganography; GPT-4 shows a capability jump in covert coordination.
locus_detail: sender-to-receiver messages carrying steganographic payload past an overseer
evaluation: CASE framework: individual capability tests and group sender-receiver-overseer tests; encoding, Schelling-point and covertext success rates; GPT-2, Llama 2 7B/70B, Mixtral, GPT-3.5, GPT-4; insider-trading case study
limitation: Authors: current models have limited steganographic capability; evaluations cover simple settings only.
evidence_note: trigger: colluding agents are set up to use steganography in group evaluations (§5, App. G); trigger_evidence_level: insider-trading case is one qualitative anecdote, not a benign condition; locus: covert messages between sender and receiver (§4, Fig. 2); defense_family: overseer detection in group evaluation, 26% evasion (§6, App. G); defense_evaluated_against: overseer tested only against instructed steganography
review_note: Insider-trading case could count as emergent (benign) collusion; chose narrower adversarial. Paraphrasing and parameter optimisation are analyzed theoretically (Thm 4), not tested, so only monitoring is coded as defense. Paper is largely formal; coded evidence as experiment.

failure_observed: Debate lowers accuracy over rounds as models switch from correct to incorrect answers under peer reasoning, even when stronger models outnumber weaker ones.
locus_detail: peer agents reasoning exchanged between debate rounds
evidence_note: trigger: harmful shifts arise from sycophancy and conformity, no attacker (abstract); trigger_evidence_level: abstract describes no adversary; locus: "response to peer reasoning" (abstract)
review_note: No PDF. Locus message-channel is inferred; one-agent (conformity inside the model) is equally plausible. Spread not coded: abstract claims decline over rounds only.

failure_observed: Attack agents turn benign agents into infected propagators that spread malicious influence through inter-agent messages; binary guards miss infected agents.
locus_detail: attack agents inserted in the MAS graph whose messages infect neighbors (prompt, tool and memory attacks)
evaluation: Prompt injection on CSQA, MMLU, GSM8K; InjecAgent tool attacks; PoisonRAG memory attacks; ASR@3 and MDSR@3; GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3-235B; chain, tree, star, random topologies; 20 and 50 agents; 6 baselines
limitation: Authors: needs synthetic training data and labels; run-time defense needs one round of dialogue to detect threats.
evidence_note: trigger: attack agents inserted and convert benign agents (§3, §5.1); trigger_evidence_level: all settings are attacks; locus: attack agents spread via messages, plus tool and memory attacks (§5.1); spread: infection keeps rising over rounds, ASR up to 20.9% at 20 agents without defense (Table 2, Fig. 2); defense_family: GNN detection then replace attackers and rehabilitate infected (§4); defense_evaluated_against: Tables 1-7 against PI, TA, MA attacks only
review_note: Main-setting agent count not found in sections read; coded not reported.

failure_observed: A specification-compliant adversary can exploit 11 protocol-level A2A gaps, such as cross-client context injection, credential harvesting through delegation chains and exfiltration via rogue agents.
locus_detail: unprotected contextId in messages, delegation-chain identity, and agent-card capability claims
evaluation: Spec formalized into 37-state, 76-transition FSM from 929 statements; precision 73.3% and F1 84.6% vs expert review; zero-shot Claude Opus 4.6 baseline found 0 confirmed
limitation: Authors: no executable multi-agent testbed yet; mitigations only partly verified and backward compatibility untested.
evidence_note: trigger: "specification-compliant adversary" exploits protocol gaps (§3.2); trigger_evidence_level: threat model is adversary only; locus: contextId, delegation chain, Agent Card claims (§6); defense_family: spec-level mitigations such as context ownership binding and skill attestation (§6); defense_evaluated_against: mitigations only checked in Alloy and TLA+ models (§6, Formal Verification), no experiment
review_note: scope: protocol-spec analysis with no running LLM multi-agent system; evidence_type experiment is the vulnerability-finding pipeline versus expert review. Mitigations were checked in Alloy and TLA+ models, not in experiments, so coded not evaluated.

failure_observed: Hallucinations originate at or are amplified by inter-agent handoffs and propagate downstream inside fluent, confident context that later agents cannot scrutinize.
locus_detail: handoff package passed from sending to receiving agent
evaluation: HalloffBench: sequential pipeline scenarios in 5 task domains; hallucination rate and token cost; baselines unmitigated, Reflexion, Multi-Agent Debate
evidence_note: trigger: hallucination in handoffs, no adversary (abstract); trigger_evidence_level: benchmark covers hallucination only (abstract); locus: "handoff boundaries" (abstract); defense_family: Handoff Verification Layer with Factual Consistency Checker (abstract); defense_evaluated_against: evaluated on HalloffBench against 3 baselines (abstract)
review_note: No PDF. Spread claimed as propagation in abstract but no measurement visible, so not reported.

framework: AutoGen (Magentic-One, Selector, Round-Robin orchestrators); CrewAI; MetaGPT
failure_observed: Adversarial web or file content hijacks control flow through an orchestrator so the system executes arbitrary malicious code or exfiltrates data, 58-100% of trials with GPT-4o.
locus_detail: untrusted file or web page read by a file or web agent whose fake-error output relays the request to the orchestrator
evaluation: Reverse-shell and exfiltration payloads; attack success rate, 10 runs per framework-orchestrator-model-input-error-query cell; GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 1.5 Pro and Flash
limitation: Reviewer: default configurations of three frameworks only; defenses discussed but not tested.
evidence_note: trigger: adversary plants content that reaches the orchestrator via a sub-agent (§4, Fig. 1); trigger_evidence_level: threat model assumes benign agents, adversary only the content (§3); locus: malicious file or web page relayed through file-access agent metadata (§4); spread: request passes file agent to orchestrator to code executor (Fig. 1, §5)
review_note: An accidental-hijack anecdote (benign file) appears in the discussion but is not an experiment, so not coded as benign trigger. Defenses are only discussed.
